We believe in holistic, cross-platform tracking to truly understand your users’ experiences, so we try to make Heap as easy to install as possible on most platforms and frameworks.
Quick install: Google Tag Manager, Instapage, Segment, Shopify, Squarespace, Shogun, Tumblr, Wix, Wordpress.
Heap virtualizes your data, so the events you choose to track can be renamed, re-organized, or even grouped with other events after the fact, retroactively.
Heap automatically captures a wealth of client-side interactions out-of-the-box, including clicks, pageviews, form submissions, and change events, with no developer work needed.
Use this API to send custom events and associated metadata to Heap that we do not automatically capture, such as purchase information, email sent, and more.
Use this API to attach a unique identity and maintain user histories across sessions, devices, and browsers under a single profile in Heap.
Use this API to reset a user’s identity to an anonymous state after they have logged out.
Use this API to send stateful information into Heap as a set of global key-value pairs that get attached to all of a user's subsequent events.
The addUserProperties API allows you to attach custom properties to your users, whether they are identified or still anonymous.
When a user is identified, their past sessions and event activity from when they were anonymous are now tied to that identity.
The underlying interactions will still be captured (ex. pageview, click) but the sensitive parts will be replaced by **** in your Heap dataset before it leaves the browser.
By adding heap-ignore to an element, you exclude an element from being tracked in its entirety, not just the sensitive part(s).
If you wish to redact the text content of elements on all pages (not locally), then you can set `disableTextCapture`.
We recommend using this for events that need to exactly match your backend, such as completed order transaction info
it takes an `events` array of objects with a max of 1000 events per request.
When this call is made, all events associated with the provided user_id are migrated to the user with the provided identity.
you should use this endpoint to send useful account properties for analysis (e.g. payment tier, account owner, account name, etc).
Submits users to be deleted from Heap, and returns a unique identifier for the request (`deletion_request_id`). Up to 10,000 users can be submitted in a single request.
Replays are automatically cued to the exact event you need. Easily track and search both client and server-side events within a replay for paths, errors, and clicked text.
Collaborate on analysis by sending replays via email directly from the player.
